audience.programmeDescription: Slavonic Language and Culture at the University of Amsterdam studies Slavic languages, literature, cultural history and contemporary Central and Eastern European societies. Students choose Russian, Polish, Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian or Czech. This example follows Russian and includes the required semester in Riga.
audience.comparisonExplanation: UCR offers substantial literary interpretation, language-processing research, cultural and historical analysis, European institutions and social inquiry. These provide real related study, including Soviet documentary history, but do not combine into sustained investigation of Slavic languages, literature and Central or Eastern European societies. Expanding these methods across a complete programme changes the focus to general humanities or European social science. The conclusion concerns the programme’s academic substance, not language acquisition alone or a professional qualification.

curriculum.routeLabel: Russian main language; Riga study abroad

componentNotes.sla-133121026y: A Dutch writing diagnostic and recurring tutoring accompany the programme. They carry no credits.
componentNotes.sla-133112016y: This example follows Russian. Polish, Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian and Czech are alternative main-language choices.
componentNotes.sla-133112036y: Complete Russian 1 and 2 before Russian 3; Russian 4 follows Russian 3. Russian 5 requires Russian 4, and Russian 6 requires Russian 5.
componentNotes.sla-133110286y: Complete A World of Regions and Russian 3 before this course, which includes historical Slavic phonology, morphology and older texts.
componentNotes.sla-133221146y: Complete the first year before Language Contact. Russian 5 and 6 and The History of Slavic provide recommended preparation.
componentNotes.sla-133221018y: The Russian pathway requires the second semester of year two at the University of Latvia in Riga. Before departure, pass at least 54 first-year EC and 18 EC from the first semester of year two, including Russian 5 and 6. The 30 EC must follow the programme’s cultural-history, linguistics/translation, literature or language-acquisition lines without duplicating home study. Language courses must exceed the stated B1 speaking/writing and B2 reading exit levels. Students unable to travel for valid reasons need Examination Board approval for a 30-EC home alternative.
componentNotes.sla-133221206y: This course requires level-three Slavic language acquisition or equivalent. The completed Russian sequence supplies the preparation.
componentNotes.sla-133219026y: Pass Russian 6, Making Sense of Aspect in Time and Space and Russian and Eastern European Literature after 1950 before the lab. It develops qualitative and quantitative language/literature research and a thesis proposal.
componentNotes.sla-approved-free-profiling-space: Thirty credits remain available for electives, a minor or an optional placement. Normally no more than 12 EC may be introductory; an approved UvA minor or one-language sequence can permit up to 24 EC. External study requires Examination Board approval, minors cannot duplicate compulsory language study, and placements occupy at most 12 EC.
componentNotes.sla-133219002y: The twelve-credit thesis is a supervised individual research project using critically evaluated primary and secondary sources. The research lab prepares its proposal. It is normally written in Dutch; a different language requires Examination Board approval. Register for the thesis and follow the programme handbook’s supervision and submission rules.
